meta.title: Chennai property-tax payment (current year, residential, known bill number) grid-only evidence ledger
meta.disclaimer: Independent research, not official advice. Grid-only benchmark run: sources and claims only, no nodes, edges, roadblocks or journeys. Desk research, no counter visited. Limitations: the corporation's published method for assessing property tax refers to a percentage table 'given above' and to location-wise basic rates 'furnished in the annexure', and neither is present on the page, which ends with the literal placeholder 'TO BE UPDATED'; the Property Tax Calculator link on the corporation's live property-tax page points to a third-party staging host over plain HTTP on a non-standard port and did not connect on the access date; the Know your Status link on the same page returned HTTP 404; the payment, status and receipt routes are public but were read only, with no zone, division, bill or sub number entered and no payment begun. Do not submit personal data through this ledger.

scenarios.label: Chennai property-tax payment on a known bill number
scenarios.summary: An individual owner pays the current year's property tax on a residential property already on the municipal register with a known identifier, by the municipal payment route, online portal first and counter or bank route second. First-time assessment, name transfer or mutation, arrears disputes, rebate eligibility beyond what the payment route itself states, and commercial property are excluded.

claims.text: The corporation's property tax rules and procedure page states that payment can be made online at www.chennaicorporation.gov.in with 'Nil' transaction fee by using a credit card, debit card or net banking.
claims.notes: An explicit zero for the online channel, recorded as a stated value under protocol section 3. It fixes the charge for using the channel, not the tax itself.

claims.text: The corporation's property tax rules and procedure page lists the modes of paying property tax.
claims.notes: A usable rule about where the tax may be paid. The cheque or demand draft instruction this claim previously also carried is recorded atomically at claim_chennai_ptax_revenue_officer_is_payee. Split during IND-91 part B lint remediation into one claim per published mode.

claims.text: One mode is payment through the tax collectors.
claims.notes: Split during IND-91 part B lint remediation from claim_chennai_ptax_payment_modes; one published mode, one claim.

claims.text: One mode is payment through eleven named banks under a walk-in payment system.
claims.notes: Split during IND-91 part B lint remediation from claim_chennai_ptax_payment_modes; one published mode, one claim.

claims.text: One mode is payment at e-seva common service centres run by Tamil Nadu Arasu Cable Television Corporation.
claims.notes: Split during IND-91 part B lint remediation from claim_chennai_ptax_payment_modes; one published mode, one claim.

claims.text: Those e-seva centres are located in taluk offices or zonal offices or divisional offices or headquarters.
claims.notes: Split during IND-91 part B lint remediation from claim_chennai_ptax_payment_modes. Where the e-seva centres sit is separately checkable from the mode itself.

claims.text: One mode is payment online.
claims.notes: Split during IND-91 part B lint remediation from claim_chennai_ptax_payment_modes; one published mode, one claim.

claims.text: The corporation's online payment and receipt routes require a zone number, a division code, a bill number and a sub number.
claims.notes: Matches this scenario's premise of a known property identifier. Split during IND-91 part B lint remediation; the instruction to confirm the bill number first is asserted separately.

claims.text: Both routes tell the citizen to ensure the property tax bill number before making payment.
claims.notes: Split during IND-91 part B lint remediation from claim_chennai_ptax_bill_number_required. The instruction is separately checkable from the fields the routes require.

claims.text: The corporation's assessment method page states that property tax in Chennai city limits is a half-yearly tax calculated as a percentage of annual rental value.
claims.notes: A half-yearly cycle, without any date on which a half year's tax falls due. Split during IND-91 part B lint remediation; how annual rental value is arrived at is asserted separately.

claims.text: That page states that the annual rental value is arrived at from the reasonable letting value under section 100 of the Chennai City Municipal Corporation Act 1919.
claims.notes: Split during IND-91 part B lint remediation from claim_chennai_ptax_half_yearly_basis. The statutory basis of the value is separately checkable from the half-yearly cycle.

claims.text: The corporation's assessment method page states that the annual value of a building is obtained by multiplying the monthly rental value by the common factor 10.92, and works the derivation through a numeric example.
claims.notes: One half of the calculation is published; the rate to apply to the annual value is not.

claims.text: The corporation's assessment method page refers the citizen to a percentage table 'given above' for the half-yearly tax.
claims.notes: Direct current observation of the page's own contents. The two missing pieces are exactly the two numbers a citizen needs to compute the tax. Split during IND-91 part B lint remediation into the two references, their absence and the page's closing text.

claims.text: The same page refers the citizen to an annexure for location-wise basic rates per square foot.
claims.notes: Split during IND-91 part B lint remediation from claim_chennai_ptax_rate_table_and_annexure_missing. The second reference is separately checkable from the first.

claims.text: Neither that table nor that annexure appears anywhere on the page.
claims.notes: Split during IND-91 part B lint remediation from claim_chennai_ptax_rate_table_and_annexure_missing. The absence is separately checkable from the references to them.

claims.text: The page ends with the text 'TO BE UPDATED'.
claims.notes: Split during IND-91 part B lint remediation from claim_chennai_ptax_rate_table_and_annexure_missing. Direct observation of the page's closing text.

claims.text: The corporation's assessment method page states that a 10 per cent library cess is calculated from the general tax component of property tax.
claims.notes: A rate that is published, applied to a base that is not. Split during IND-91 part B lint remediation; the authorities cited are asserted separately.

claims.text: That page cites G.O.Ms.No.492 of 19.05.1992 and Council Resolution No.246/2001 of 22.05.2001 for the library cess.
claims.notes: Split during IND-91 part B lint remediation from claim_chennai_ptax_library_cess. The authorities cited are separately checkable from the rate.

claims.text: The corporation publishes a Property Tax Online Payment Receipt route that is reachable without login.
claims.notes: The observation is the route, its title and its four input fields on the access date. No identifier was entered, no login was used and no case data was retrieved. Split during IND-91 part B lint remediation; what the route returns is asserted separately.

claims.text: That route returns a payment receipt for a property identified by those four bill fields.
claims.notes: Split during IND-91 part B lint remediation from claim_chennai_ptax_public_receipt_route. The four fields are the ones asserted by claim_chennai_ptax_bill_number_required. The inference is what the route returns for a real property, since no identifier was entered and no case data was retrieved.

claims.text: The corporation publishes a Property Tax Status route and a Property Tax Payment Status route alongside the payment route, all reachable without login.
claims.notes: The routes were observed as published links and entry forms; neither was exercised.

claims.text: The corporation's payment and receipt routes both carry a note directing a citizen with any discrepancy in their property tax to submit complaints with particulars to the Revenue Officer.
claims.notes: A named role with a direct contact route, published on the payment surface itself. Institutional contact details only. Split during IND-91 part B lint remediation; the telephone numbers are asserted separately.

claims.text: That note gives telephone numbers 2538 3614 and 2538 4510 extension 370 for the Revenue Officer.
claims.notes: Split during IND-91 part B lint remediation from claim_chennai_ptax_revenue_officer_contact. The contact numbers are separately checkable from the routing instruction. Institutional contact details only.

claims.text: The corporation's property tax rules and procedure page names 'The Revenue Officer, Corporation of Chennai' as the payee in whose favour a cheque or demand draft for property tax must be drawn.
claims.notes: The same role the discrepancy note points to, identified from a second route.

claims.text: The Property Tax Calculator link on the corporation's live property tax section index points to a third-party staging host, coc-staging.egovernments.org, over plain HTTP on port 9980.
claims.notes: Recorded as observed. The calculator is the route that would supply the missing rate, so its failure and the missing table are the same gap seen twice. Split during IND-91 part B lint remediation; the connection failure is asserted separately.

claims.text: That address did not connect on the access date.
claims.notes: Split during IND-91 part B lint remediation from claim_chennai_ptax_calculator_points_to_staging_host. The failure is separately checkable from where the link points.

claims.text: The Know your Status link on the corporation's property tax section index returned HTTP 404 on the access date.
The corporation's property tax rules and procedure page publishes a document list for the submission of an application for assessment of property tax.
claims.notes: Recorded to mark the boundary with this scenario's excluded first-assessment route, not to support the documents cell. Split during IND-91 part B lint remediation into the list, its contents and its scope.

claims.text: That list comprises registered documents in the applicant's favour or a filled application Form-6 or the last tax paid receipt.
claims.notes: Split during IND-91 part B lint remediation from claim_chennai_ptax_assessment_documents_are_other_route. What the list contains is separately checkable from what it is for.

claims.text: That document list is not given for paying tax on an existing assessment.
claims.notes: Split during IND-91 part B lint remediation from claim_chennai_ptax_assessment_documents_are_other_route. The scope limit is the reason this claim does not support the documents cell of this scenario.

claims.text: The date on which a half year's property tax falls due is not established by any reviewed public page.
claims.notes: Retained because the uncertainty itself matters to the journey. Not login-related; the payment route is public. Split during IND-91 part B lint remediation; the penalty and rebate unknown is asserted separately.

claims.text: Whether any penalty or rebate attaches to paying late or early is not established by any reviewed public page.
claims.notes: Split during IND-91 part B lint remediation from claim_chennai_ptax_due_date_unknown. Retained because the uncertainty itself matters to the journey. Not login-related.

claims.text: The amount of property tax payable on a residential property for the current half year cannot be derived from any reviewed public page.
claims.notes: Retained because the uncertainty itself matters to the journey. Not login-related; the calculator that would answer it points at an unreachable staging host. The observed reason is carried by claim_chennai_ptax_rate_table_and_annexure_missing_3, which records that neither the percentage table nor the annexure appears anywhere on the page that cites them.
